item.title: Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month.
item.description:
Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month.
From October 13 to October 20, Arc Raiders will have a PvE toggle, allowing you to seamlessly switch between lobbies where you can fight other players and lobbies where players can't do damage to you. The aim is to give players more choice and test the ability to let players completely disengage from PvP gameplay. As a result, loot in PvE will be lower-valued because the mode has lower stakes. Additionally, ARCs will target downed players to create some form of tension, but if players stay still, they will be ignored by AI foes.
Embark will be monitoring the player economy and matchmaking times during this period. The team has noted that "it's possible that this will not work," meaning PvE may not actually make its way into the game permanently. This is a test to see how well they can make it'll operate, rather than some kind of stress test.
"It’s important to mention that this is not a risk-free test," said the studio. "The first, unlaunched iteration of ARC Raiders was conceived as a PvE game, and we have been hesitant to return to that concept. There is a risk that introducing a PvE matchmaking toggle could reduce some of the tension that the game was built around. At the same time, we have to respect that some players want to enjoy the game in their own way, and we can’t ignore what the data is telling us.
"As creators, we design a game with an intention for how we think it should be played; but after launch, it becomes the players’ game. This is one of the unique and wonderful things about making games; we build something with a specific vision, and then we get to see players finding their own ways to enjoy it."
The reason for the test is that Embark Studios' data demonstrated that a sizable amount of players ignored or tried to avoid combat against other players. They were more interested in a co-op, social experience rather than one where they had to fight real humans. You can view some of the data directly from Embark below.
It'll be interesting to see what comes of this test and it's refreshing to see a studio experimenting with something so publicly, even if it doesn't result in any permanent changes. Either way, the community will have to show whether it wants Arc Raiders to have PvE or not and provide actionable feedback to make it feasible.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history.
item.description:
Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history.
Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson says the project was internally titled Goliath, so as to appropriately echo the size and scale of what Ubisoft Milan hoped to achieve with the game. It was an ambitious plan, and one that former Ubisoft developer Gian Marco Zanna described as a “new big bang in the video game universe.”
This description, while dramatic, is accurate; Ubisoft Milan’s Zelda game would have been drastically different from anything we’ve seen from the series thus far. Rather than following Link’s adventures in the wilds of Hyrule, it would have been a spin-off title in the broader Zelda universe featuring a brand-new, “never-before-seen character.”
However, during its early concept phase, Nintendo reportedly asked that this protagonist be changed to the franchise’s ultimate big bad: Ganondorf. This would have been the first time Ganondorf was the central, playable character in a Zelda game, and on paper, it sounds like a fantastic idea… but unfortunately, it didn’t end up coming to fruition.
Sources told Henderson that Ubisoft Milan was given a deadline of late 2023 to come up with a prototype for this Ganondorf game, but Nintendo reportedly rejected their proposal when the time came, for reasons that have not been made clear.
Ubisoft Milan was behind the highly-lauded Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, which IGN scored a sparkling nine out of 10. The studio reportedly began ideation for Goliath shortly after its release, clearly riding the high of its successful launch. It’s almost painful to imagine the game we could’ve had; perhaps it was a Ganon origin story?
Given that it was a spin-off and not a sequel or prequel, it’s unclear what, exactly, Ganon would be doing in this game. And what about Ubisoft Milan’s first intended protagonist for the project?
We have so many questions, and it’s likely that none of them will ever get answered. Ubisoft did not respond to Henderson’s requests for comment, but he did note that it had internally acknowledged a journalist requesting information about Goliath beforehand.
Among the oodles of canceled, top-secret games over the years, this one definitely makes us go down the ‘what if’ rabbit hole. It’s almost as tantalizing as the canceled Disney Smash Bros.-style game, which former concept artist Ken Christiansen shared artwork for on his personal online portfolio, showing characters like Captain Hook, the Sheriff of Nottingham, the Queen of Hearts, John Silver, and others facing off in 2v2 battles.

item.title: Dressmaker, an indie game where you run a boutique and design dresses, is taking over Steam, becoming one of the platform’s Top 10 best-selling games mere days after its release.
item.description:
Dressmaker, an indie game where you run a boutique and design dresses, is taking over Steam, becoming one of the platform’s Top 10 best-selling games mere days after its release.
If you’re on gaming Twitter, you’ve likely come across clips from a game where players are carefully stitching together fabric to make ornate gowns. That’s no coincidence; Dressmaker, the game in question, is having a moment right now, and Steam’s best sellers list proves it.
At the time of writing this article on September 24, Dressmaker has reached tenth place on Steam’s Top Sellers list. It’s also earned an Overwhelmingly Positive rating, with 96% of 2,177 user reviews being positive.
Dressmaker has beaten out massive titles like Diablo IV and even had the upper hand over Marvel Rivals for a moment. Its popularity is sparking a wave of interest in the game, as well as starting an interesting conversion on social media regarding smaller games that are made to suit a niche audience versus big-budget, AAA titles designed to appeal to as many players as possible.
One Twitter/X user described it best: “Take game marketed towards women and creatives / optimise it so it can run on most shitty laptops and PCs that have been sold in the last 10 years / fill it with whimsy and genuine respect for the craft it’s emulating / make a billion dollars.’
“Hey look, a niche game appealing directly to a target audience that loves it. Amazing,” another wrote, comparing the game to AAA titles that “look so generic I can’t tell them apart.”
“We need more of this! Make more games targeting specific audiences instead of bastardizing successful IPs to fit ‘everybody,’” another said.
Dressmaker was developed by Cozy Lives and published by Free Lives, an independent game studio based in Cape Town, South Africa that’s behind games like Genital Jousting and Terra Nil.
In Dressmaker, players own and operate their very own dress boutique, where they design and sew dresses for customers in a fictional town. It’s not just a dress-up game, though; you can also “sabotage” your clientele if you want to make the stakes a little higher.
This is the latest indie game to go viral on social media following Stray Dog: nobody cares, a Soulslike game where you play as a stray dog on a quest to rescue its master using an old, rusty sword it wields in its jaws.

item.title: Microsoft has stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders are “heavily skewed” toward PlayStation 5 over Xbox Series X and S.
item.description:
Microsoft has stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders are “heavily skewed” toward PlayStation 5 over Xbox Series X and S.
In a report about this week’s layoffs and studios reorganization at Xbox, The Verge’s Tom Warren said the PS5’s dominance over GTA 6 preorders was “ringing yet more alarm bells" about Xbox as a platform.
However, Xbox CSO Matthew Ball insisted that Microsoft was “very happy” with GTA 6 preorders, and that its internal data showed preorders were matching “our share of the console market.”
Here’s Ball’s statement in full:
“Tom, we are very happy with GTA VI pre-orders. The title is breaking records for XBOX, we expect even more records will be broken throughout the fall, and our internal analysis shows our share of preorders to be matching our share of the console market.”
While Sony does announce PS5 sales, Microsoft hasn’t announced a number for Xbox Series X and S sales in years. As of June 30, PS5 had sold more than 95 million units. Analysts have suggested the combined Xbox Series range is being outsold by the PS5 by at least a factor of 2:1. If that ratio holds true, there are likely twice as many GTA 6 preorders for PS5 than for Xbox Series X and S.
Sony and Rockstar Games' partnership for GTA 6 wil be having a big impact on preorders, too. Sony has leaned heavily into GTA 6, which you can understand given we’re talking about a video game that is expected to break sales records and spark a surge in console sales. This has led to GTA 6 gameplay focusing on the PS5 version, the PS5 showing up in marketing materials for GTA 6, and even a custom GTA 6 UI for Sony’s console.
Sony has published blog posts talking about the features of the PS5 that GTA 6 will use, such as the speaker in the DualSense controller and the pad's haptic feedback. Other additions to GTA 6's PS5 marketing campaign include a version of the PlayStation app logo on smartphones that features GTA 6 colors and pale tree fronds. So, with PlayStation’s partnership in full swing, preorders being “heavily skewed” toward PS5 shouldn’t come as much of a surprise to anyone.
The Verge’s report also suggested that the Xbox “reset,” led by new CEO Asha Sharma, might be about making Xbox easier to spin off or operate as a wholly owned subsidiary, as has been suggested by prior reports elsewhere.
GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S only on November 19.

item.title: The next Saw movie has officially hired a director as it prepares for Jigsaw's next game.
item.description:
The next Saw movie has officially hired a director as it prepares for Jigsaw's next game.
Mike P. Nelson, an up-and-coming horror director responsible for films like the Wrong Turn reboot and Silent Night, Deadly Night, has been selected to direct the next Saw film. The flick is being penned by Gregory Weidman & Geoff Tock and produced by horror legends James Wan, Jason Blum, and Leigh Whannell. Wan and Whannell created the series as a disturbing short film before eventually expanding it into a gory low-budget feature.
Wan largely moved on from Saw following the third film, going on to direct Insidious, The Conjuring, and blockbusters like Aquaman. He's expected to have a much more significant role in the next installment as Lionsgate attempts to bolster the franchise once again. Speaking on the decision to select Nelson as the director of the next chapter, Wan praised his style of filmmaking.
did you miss me? pic.twitter.com/c6tpQwanFF
“Making the original Saw was a defining experience for me, so it was essential to find a director who would honor that world," said Wan. "Mike has a raw, distinctive filmmaking voice with an inventive approach to the genre, and I believe he’ll bring something truly unique and special to the franchise.”
Nelson was also excited about being able to take a crack at the beloved franchise.
“Being asked to play in this twisted sandbox with James is nothing short of a dream come true," said Nelson. "Greg and Geoff and James have crafted such a wild script that brings the mystery of the original while exploring new insane bloody ideas that meld so well with the brutal moral compass of the franchise. Let the games begin!”
It's unclear exactly what the next Saw film will entail. Saw X left the door open for more prequel movies, following Jigsaw's adventures prior to his death, but creative disagreements reportedly caused the film to stall out. The various creatives that worked on Saw X were expected to return for a sequel, but have since walked away from the franchise. As a result, it sounds like whatever comes next will be something very different.
Wan and Whannell did confirm to Bloody Disgusting earlier this year that Jigsaw will play a significant role in the next Saw film, despite his death in the third movie.
"Leigh and I, we’re not going to give too much away, but we don’t think you can make a Saw movie without Jigsaw. That’s the bottom line. And ultimately, we want to hark back to the spirit, what Leigh and I love about the original first movie. The original first movie, which is Jigsaw’s philosophy and what makes him tick."
A new Saw video game is also in the works from Bloober Team. The game, titled Saw: Genesis, is a multiplayer game where three players must escape a series of deadly games while a fourth player manipulates traps and tries to find ways to kill the victims.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Players who haven’t yet experienced Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown can play the entire game for free right now on Nintendo Switch and the Nintendo Switch 2 until September 30.
item.description:
Players who haven’t yet experienced Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown can play the entire game for free right now on Nintendo Switch and the Nintendo Switch 2 until September 30.
Ubisoft Montpellier's 2D Metroidvania-style Prince of Persia game can be downloaded for free in its entirety as a playable demo starting at 10 AM PT today, September 24, through Wednesday, September 30 at 11:59 PM PT.
You’ll need to be a Nintendo Switch Online member to take advantage of this wild offer, though. There’s more to it than just the game, too, though that in itself is a massive deal; members can also earn 100 My Nintendo Platinum Points by completing a mission in the game during this trial period.
For more information on how to score these points, you can check out the Missions & Rewards section on the Nintendo Switch Online portal or from your Nintendo Switch’s home screen. And like many other modern game demos, you’ll be able to carry over your save data from this trial if you end up buying the full game.
If you haven’t played it yet, it’s definitely worth a try; we at IGN scored the game a glowing eight out of 10, praising the title for capturing “not only what made games such as The Sands of Time so good,” but also ironing out “the little issues that plagued the 3D games in this series by opting for a 2D perspective.”
It’s a refreshing take on the iconic series, and one that’s well worth a shot — but despite receiving critical acclaim, Ubisoft disbanded the team behind the game after it failed to meet sales expectations, and plans for a sequel were also reportedly scrapped in favor of putting its developers on other projects (like Beyond Good and Evil 2, which is still in development and recently added a writer from Assassin's Creed Shadows to its ranks).
Since then, the game has received a few new modes, updates, story DLC, and even a mobile port, though the possibility of a sequel remains grim. There’s hope that renewed interest in the title, thanks to free demos like this one and multiple big sales over the years, could sway Ubisoft’s opinion… but it’s not looking likely.
If you are planning on playing The Lost Crown, check out our Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown 100% Walkthrough and our handy interactive map and checklist tool. It's a really big little game and these tips and tricks are also a great place to start.
At least fans have The Rogue Prince of Persia, which received a fair few updates this year like new elements, tools, weapons affixes, and other quality-of-life improvements; though the highly-anticipated Sands of Time remake has unfortunately been canned.

item.title: Robert Pattinson has trouble imagining a universe where his Batman and James Gunn's Superman could co-exist, casting doubt on a potential crossover.
item.description:
Robert Pattinson has trouble imagining a universe where his Batman and James Gunn's Superman could co-exist, casting doubt on a potential crossover.
Speaking with LADbible, Pattinson stated that he thinks it would be difficult to pluck his take on a dark, grounded Batman and drop him in James Gunn's lighter, more fantastical DC universe.
“I think it would be kind of tough to have this version of Bruce outside of that world," he said. "It's one of the only characters, I guess because of the length of the shoots, but also it's such a specific kind of [style], the tone of it gets inside you. I remember that happened to me the last time I did it, it took a while. You’re just in the dark, the whole time. Both mood-wise and light-wise, I can't see anything for like months. It does affect you, like you feel strange afterwards."
Fans have been somewhat split for a while now over whether Pattinson should also play Batman in Gunn's main DC universe, or if he should remain relegated to his own separate part of the multiverse, and it seems like Pattinson believes the latter makes the most sense. James Gunn himself has said that they're developing a Batman film that will follow an older Bruce Wayne, with Damian Wayne as his sidekick.
There have been very few updates about that film, with some believing DC may wait for Matt Reeves to conclude his story before introducing another Batman in order to avoid confusing audiences. Of course, plans could change at any minute, and they could choose to leverage Pattinson's Batman in the DCU. Despite the major difference in tone between The Batman and Gunn's Superman, the current DCU does have some darker stories on offer.
Lanterns is proof that a grounded and more mature story can still easily fit into the larger DCU. Next month, we'll also get Clayface, which is set to be an R-rated body horror film set in the same universe as Superman, Lanterns, and Supergirl. There's room for a bit of everything, and some think that the strong contrast between Pattinson's Batman and David Corenswet's Superman could provide for a charming take on World's Finest.
Maybe one day it will all happen, but if Pattinson's comments are anything to go by, it won't be anytime soon. The Batman Part 2 hits theaters on February 18, 2027. Man of Tomorrow, the sequel to Superman, will fly into theaters on July 9, 2027.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Jacob Batalon shed some light on what Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton likes most about Naruto, giving fans a tentative idea of the direction his live-action adaptation of the iconic anime series might take.
item.description:
Jacob Batalon shed some light on what Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton likes most about Naruto, giving fans a tentative idea of the direction his live-action adaptation of the iconic anime series might take.
Jacob Batalon, who plays Peter Parker’s bestie Ned Leeds in the Tom Holland films, sat down for an episode of The Anime Effect podcast with Crunchyroll on September 19 to chat about all things anime.
Naturally, the topic of Destin Daniel Cretton’s live-action Naruto movie came up, prompting the hosts to quiz him about what the Brand New Day director likes best about the classic anime.
Speaking from his own perspective, Batalon said that he feels like Cretton is drawn to the origin story of Team 7 — the main group of characters in the original Naruto series, initially made up of Naruto, Sasuke, Sakura, and its leader, Kakashi.
“I think he likes the aspect of Team 7 and their coming-up story,” he explained. “I think that’s really cool. I think for a lot of storytelling in movies, when you’re trying to move from a specific IP to movies meant for everyone, you have to start somewhere where everyone kind of understands where they’re coming from. I think a lot of origin story-type things are really important when you’re trying to tell a story that not everyone is accustomed to.
“I think that could be a main thing. But also, he’s been doing this for a long time. I have no idea what he’s doing now. He could’ve completely changed it all and probably made Orochimaru the main character. I don’t know. He could've done something crazy,” he laughed.
While Batalon made it clear that he isn’t certain how Cretton’s movie will actually pan out, it wouldn’t be surprising if we saw him adapt Team 7’s come-up journey; centering on the main group of characters and following their storyline would make sense, especially since certain actors are already reportedly in talks to take on the roles of some of Team 7’s members.
For instance, Charles Melton was reported to be in final negotiations to play Kakashi in August, choosing to move away from X-Men’s Beast in Marvel Studios’ upcoming reboot film.
The search for Naruto is still underway, though. An open casting call was put out this summer, reportedly looking for young male actors between 16 and 20 years old who are “athletic, energetic, expressive” and speak fluent English.
Masashi Kishimoto, the mangaka who created Naruto, has stated that he is extremely excited about the movie, writing a statement on the series’ official website saying he “cannot believe” his manga is being adapted into a major Hollywood film.
“Right now, miracles are happening to me, one after another. My work, Naruto, is truly, truly becoming a Hollywood movie! And an even greater miracle is that the film will be directed by the one and only Destin Daniel Cretton. I still cannot believe it!” he said.
Image Credits: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images / Masashi Kishimoto / Shueisha

item.title: It's no secret that Marathon has had a rough time since launching in March 2026, but Bungie is hard at work on new game modes that it's hoping will breathe new life into the game.
item.description:
It's no secret that Marathon has had a rough time since launching in March 2026, but Bungie is hard at work on new game modes that it's hoping will breathe new life into the game.
Prevously, Bungie teased that new game modes were coming to Marathon, and even released an 'experimental' mode with Vault Breaker. Today, the company posted on Twitter detailing the new ways people can play game. The Extraction modes that it was launched with aren't going anywhere, but Bungie will be adding a team deathmatch mode, along with new PvE modes that should be reminiscent of Destiny. Bungie will also be expanding Perimeter, essentially its tutorial level, to be closer in scope to other full zones.
Bungie's goal seems to be limiting the friction that new players feel and letting them filter themselves into more familiar gameplay types. That should, in theory, let people ease themselves into the traditional extraction mode that's proven so divisive.
https://t.co/SKfaCog1Aw
All of this new content and game modes aren't going to come at the same time, though. In its post, Bungie laid out a road map, with a Nightfall refresh coming first in October. Then, in December, there will be the Symbiosis update, which will bring Marathon's first permanent PvE mode, along with Team Deathmatch. Bungie doesn't go into a lot of detail on what this new PvE mode will look like, but says it will give more details closer to launch.
In March, which will mark Marathon's one-year anniversary, Bungie is planning a much larger update that will apparently link all of these gameplay modes together. There will also be a new onboarding experience, which the company previewed a little bit in a behind-the-scenes documentary that dropped earlier today. There will even be a giant Tick Queen.
All of these updates seem like a promising way to bring players back to Marathon, but only time will tell if it's enough. Either way, Bungie will be returning to Destiny, starting with returning vaulted content back to Destiny 2. Beyond that, it seems like fans have convinced Bungie to return to Destiny long-term, with developer Poria Torkan saying, "Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it. It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny."
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: In an interview with game consultant Indie Game Joe, Counter-Strike co-creator Minh Le revealed a hilarious anecdote about Valve boss Gabe Newell that’s going viral for just how absurd it is.
item.description:
In an interview with game consultant Indie Game Joe, Counter-Strike co-creator Minh Le revealed a hilarious anecdote about Valve boss Gabe Newell that’s going viral for just how absurd it is.
Le claimed that, at one point during his tenure, Newell became so enamored with the concept of Mongolian throat singing that he couldn’t stop practicing it in Valve’s corporate offices — to the point where his employees started closing their office doors to avoid the noise.
If you’re not familiar with Mongolian throat singing, it’s a vocal technique most popularly associated with the people of Tuvan, a region in Russia located northwest of Mongolia. The Tuvan people call it Khöömei, and it’s achieved by using circular breathing to produce two or more notes simultaneously. It’s a seriously impressive talent that has become popularized over time, and has been utilized in a number of famous films and TV series (like the Sardaukar chant in the first Dune movie, for example).
Apparently, Newell wanted to try it out for himself — but his choice to practice in the workplace wasn’t necessarily conducive to a collaborative work environment.
“At one point, he got into Mongolian throat singing,” Le explained. “In Mongolia, they have these throat singers that sing really interestingly, just using their throats. Gabe watched this documentary on them. He got really fascinated with this concept, and he started to practice that. He was doing it throughout the office. He would just walk around the halls doing this throat-singing thing.
“You would hear him try to sing with his throat as he’s walking down the hall. I remember a lot of the people in the office were kind of annoyed with this, because, you know, it's kind of loud, right? …He would do it daily. People would just start closing their doors. It started to become quite a closed office. It was an interesting time. Thankfully, he didn’t do it for more than — I think it lasted for about five months.”
As pointed out by a commenter on Instagram, Le isn’t the only Valve veteran to have mentioned Gabe’s Mongolian throat singing phase; in the Half-Life 2: 20th Anniversary Documentary, senior developer Charlie Brown mentioned that the office was “normally pretty vibrant and loud,” with staff “riding scooters in the hallway and doing all sorts of stuff,” while Gabe was “Tuvan throat singing.”
Fans can watch the man practicing for themselves in the Dota 2 Mega-Kills Announcement Pack video on YouTube, which shows him warming up a sound booth as part of a skit.
Unsurprisingly, Le’s most recent story has resulted in no end of jokes and memes about Gabe’s Mongolian throat singing phase, with fans joking that he “yearns for the steppe” and affectionately dubbing him “Gabe-is Khan.”
This is the latest amusing news to come from Newell after he purchased a $70.8 million super mansion in June, which came with its own underground tunnel. You know, in case the Headcrabs try to get him or something.

item.title: GTA 6 fans aren't thrilled about a $400 collector's set that doesn't include the game, and they're even comparing it to previous Rockstar collector's editions.
item.description:
GTA 6 fans aren't thrilled about a $400 collector's set that doesn't include the game, and they're even comparing it to previous Rockstar collector's editions.
Rockstar Games just announced a $400 collector's set for GTA 6, which includes a bunch of premium merch, but excludes an actual copy of the game. Naturally, this has caused a bit of a ruckus online, with fans believing it lacks enough value to justify the cost. It has also drawn comparisons to other Rockstar collector's editions, including the one for GTA 5 and a similar collector's set for Red Dead Redemption 2.
The GTA 6 set includes a variety of big-ticket items that likely drove up the overall price, including a pair of Oakley sunglasses. Oakley's sunglasses often cost anywhere between $150–$200, so a custom pair likely resulted in a higher price tag for this collection. With that said, it is by far the most expensive Rockstar collector's edition to exist, and even diehard fans aren't willing to open their wallets.
"I hate to say it, but I think I’m gonna pass on the collector’s edition," said one fan. "$400 is just insane and it doesn’t even come with a steelbook copy of the game. I’d rather save my money and buy some individual merch items that look cool rather than some overpriced sunglasses."
Another fan noted that, a decade ago, GTA 6 would've had a much cheaper, yet still premium special edition that included the game as well as some of these items: "If this was 2016, they’d have an Ultimate Edition for $129.99 that includes the game, the coke mirror, the snuff spoon, the razor keychain and a map, but we live in 2026 SuperHell."
Red Dead Redemption 2 had a similar collector's box without the game that cost $100, which included various trinkets and replicas of in-game items, such as a physical version of the store catalog. Some believe that Rockstar did a far better job with that set, given it had a ton of interesting merchandise without making players break the bank.
"I would’ve actually preferred a GTA 6 Collector’s Box similar to the one for Red Dead Redemption 2," said a fan. "It felt more connected to the game and the price point of around 100 bucks was also WAY MORE reasonable."
Rockstar's western sequel also had two smaller-scale special editions, priced at $79.99 and $99.99, respectively. The former included a special physical map and digital content for the story mode, while the latter included everything in the previous edition as well as a steelbook and special online content. Although GTA 6's $100 Ultimate Edition boasts a ton of extra digital content, it won't entitle you to any kind of steelbook, a disc, or other physical goodies.
One other point of contention with fans is that the $400 collector's set for GTA 6 boasts a special physical version of Leonida's map. Historically, Rockstar has bundled a poster/map with previous GTA and Red Dead games. It's currently unclear if the standard boxed copy of GTA 6 will include a map, but IGN has reached out to Rockstar for clarification. Still, the lack of clarity at the moment hasn't stopped fans from fearing the worst.
"I remember this used to come with the normal physical copy of the game," expressed one concerned fan.
GTA 5 also had a lucrative set of special editions, with a $79.99 version that boasted a steelbook, blueprint map of San Andreas, digital content, and yes, a physical copy of the game. There was also a much larger $150 version which featured all of the content in the previous version, as well as a New Era 9FIFTY snapback hat, a secruity deposit bag with a GTA 5-themed key, and a hefty, premium box to store everything in.
Although GTA 6 won't release on a disc, it will get a physical edition that includes a code in the box. Physical copies will release on November 12, a week before launch, to allow players to pre-load the game. Rockstar is also selling a physical CD and vinyl of GTA 6's album and limited edition DualSense controllers for superfans.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Former Dragon Age exec Mark Darrah has revealed what he'd change about BioWare's beloved fantasy series, after spending more than 20 years at the studio.
item.description:
Former Dragon Age exec Mark Darrah has revealed what he'd change about BioWare's beloved fantasy series, after spending more than 20 years at the studio.
Darrah was a director or executive producer on all of the Dragon Age series, though departed the company back in 2021, years before the final version of Dragon Age: The Veilguard launched. He returned as a consultant on the game in 2023, in time for its final stretch of development.
Now, looking back on the franchise's four main games via a Q&A posted on TikTok, Darrah has reflected on what he would recommend ditching or adding to each title in an ideal world, if he were making the games all over again.
"I would be tempted to cut or dramatically reduce the dream sequence content in the Mage Tower," Darrah began, discussing Dragon Age: Origins' rather lengthy sojourn into the Fade that he admitted felt like "filler." Continuing, he added: "It's not great content, and it was definitely done pretty fast in the end."
Conversely, Darrah said he'd like to add in some extra character options, with another human origin, and potentially the Avvar.
For Dragon Age 2, Darrah said he'd address the game's ending, where players are forced to pick a side between the templars and the mages. Whichever you pick, however, things do not go well for the mage's Orsino, while the templar's leader Meredith is proven correct — and the whole thing feels less like a proper choice at all.
"[I'd change it so] if you side with the mages that you don't fight Orsino," Darrah decided. "Because essentially it makes Meredith right. My feeling is Dragon Age 2 ends with, no what you choose, Meredith is right because the mages lose control."
Moving onto Dragon Age: Inquisition, and there's no surprises here that Darrah would change the game's "crit path" — its route through the core, critical story missions — to flow faster, with less time spent in the dreaded Hinterlands. Darrah also said he'd likely excise one of the game's zones entirely, as Inquisition was unnecessarily lengthy.
"I'd probably cut Hissing Wastes maybe, or one of the big levels," Darrah mused. "It's too big. And the other thing I would change is to dramatically reduce the amount of power you need to go on crit path missions. That's there for not super great reasons, and I think you could cut it by 40-60% and the game would just be paced better.
"Also, to make sure you ship with the thing we added later which tells you to leave the first level and actually go into the game." Here, most players would likely agree.
Finally, Darrah addressed Dragon Age: The Veilguard, and had a succinct answer for what else he would include. "I would add the Keep," he said, referring to BioWare's previous cloud-based repository for players' choices throughout the franchise so far. "I told them to. It wouldn't take... that much. I mean, it would," he admitted. As for what he'd remove from Veilguard, Darrah said he did not have an answer.
What's next for Dragon Age? Very little, it seems. BioWare is now a single-project studio and entirely focused on building the next Mass Effect game, which is still years away.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Call of Duty: Warzone is getting a new Operator Skin toggle, which means you can finally turn off all those goofy skins.
item.description:
Call of Duty: Warzone is getting a new Operator Skin toggle, which means you can finally turn off all those goofy skins.
Activision said that from Season 1 of the upcoming Modern Warfare 4, this new Operator Skin toggle will be available to let players see only Modern Warfare 4 Operators in the game.
When the toggle is on, you see a Modern Warfare 4 Operator in place of any Operator or Operator Skin from another Call of Duty game that's been equipped by another player. This applies to enemies, party members, and squadmates, both in the lobby and during a match, Activision said in a blog post.
Your own equipped Operator won’t change, so you’ll continue to see the Operator you selected, even if it’s from another game. The toggle only impacts your game, not the experience of others, and will be OFF by default.
Operators and Weapons from Modern Warfare 2, Modern Warfare 3, Black Ops 6, and Black Ops 7 will remain available in Warzone starting with Season 1, including the Skins, Blueprints, and Camos you’ve earned and bought for them. “The collection you’ve built remains yours to use, and existing plans for Carry Forward for previous titles are not affected with this update,” Activision said.
“Over the last few years, Call of Duty: Warzone has brought together Operators, weapons, and experiences from across recent Call of Duty titles in one shared experience,” Activision continued. “We know some players enjoy that variety, while others would prefer Call of Duty: Warzone feel more aligned with the world of the latest release, including the upcoming Modern Warfare 4.
This is big news for Call of Duty fans, many of whom had complained about goofy skins particularly in Black Ops 6. With the likes of Beavis and Butt-Head and American Dad hitting Black Ops 6 shortly after weed-obsessed bundles starring Seth Rogen, some fans said they’d had enough of what they called the 'Fortnite-ification' of their beloved Call of Duty, and pleaded with publisher Activision to return to its mil-sim roots. Those complaints sparked a U-turn at Activision for last year's Black Ops 7, amid pressure from rival shooter Battlefield 6 and its commitment to “gritty realism.”
In May, Infinity Ward told fans to "keep the receipts" after promising to remain grounded regarding cosmetics in Modern Warfare 4.
But why not add this toggle in Black Ops 6? In a social media post, Activision insisted the toggle "required new tech that will only be available starting with Season 01."
Back with Warzone, Activision said all weapons from Modern Warfare 2 through Black Ops 7 will continue to be accessible through the Legacy tab in the Loadout menu of Call of Duty: Warzone. While these Weapons remain available to use, Gunsmith functionality and prior Custom Loadouts will not be supported for legacy Weapons or legacy Blueprints. However, these won’t be left as base Weapons without Attachments; instead a five-attachment version of each legacy base Weapon will be available, as well as any Blueprint for a legacy Weapon with their existing Attachment setups.
“Our goal for this chapter of Call of Duty: Warzone is for the weapon meta to feel distinctly rooted in Modern Warfare 4, while preserving access to nostalgic choices that players know and love,” Activision said. “Raven Software will continue to deliver on its commitment to balancing weapons on a biweekly basis, keeping the MW4 weapon lineup fluid and interesting throughout each season.”
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Starbucks has revealed a new Pokémon collection that will be coming to stores across Japan later this month.
item.description:
Starbucks has revealed a new Pokémon collection that will be coming to stores across Japan later this month.
The collection, which follows Pokémon's 30th anniversary collabs with everything from Adidas to Krispy Kreme, will feature a Pikachu-themed latte as well as a new batch of merchandise. The full spread includes over 40 new products, ranging from tumblers and mugs to aprons, totes, and even gift cards.
While the Pikachu latte will only be available in person, select merch will also be offered through the Starbucks JP online store. Unfortunately, there’s no word on whether the collaboration will be available outside of Japan.
On September 30, Starbucks locations across Japan will debut the Pikachu Honey Cream Latte, a recipe selected through a nationwide competition that received over 700 submissions. The winning recipe was submitted by Junko Nitta of Starbucks Coffee Koriyama Asaka.
The latte is flavored with a mix of honey and caramel and colored after the electric Pokemon’s iconic yellow hue. Honey-flavored whip cream tops the drink, with red heart sprinkles mimicking Pikachu’s rosy cheeks.
The Pikachu Honey Cream Latte will only be available in a size Tall, retailing for around 690 yen (US $4.34). Some reports suggest the limited-time latte will only be available for as short as nine days, from September 30 to October 8.
Starbucks JP will also be releasing a line of tumblers, totes, aprons, and even new gift cards. The 41-piece collection will be a mix of online and in-store exclusives. Given ongoing stock and scalping concerns across all things Pokémon, Starbucks will reportedly be limiting transactions for the first couple days of the release.
Hikaru Ichijo provided 12 new illustrations for the collection, which show popular Pokémon enjoying pleasant moments and building friendships with their baristas. Even Pokémon need caffeine, I suppose. The featured Pokémon shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise, with most designs featuring Pikachu, Eevee, or one of the Gen 1 starters (Charmander, Bulbasaur, and Squirtle).
The illustrations are based on a collection of “stories,” which are themselves written on some of the designs. Some quotes include “Our adventure starts with a cup of coffee,” and “Crafting wonders with you.”
Starbucks is no stranger to collaborations, and North American stores will soon be getting their own limited-edition collection themed after the Peanuts franchise. Alas, that does not mean all is looking bright for the coffee shop giant. Starbucks also just announced that they will be closing 250 stores across North America by the end of the week, presumably part of the company's ongoing "Back to Starbucks" turnaround strategy.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still in development, and just added another writer to its team.
item.description:
Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still in development, and just added another writer to its team.
18 years on from its initial announcement and a decade on from its re-announcement at E3 2016, Ubisoft is still plugging away on its sci-fi fantasy sequel — though there's still no word on when the game will actually release.
That said, work is clearly continuing. Just this week, Ubisoft Bordeaux's lead writer/associate narrative director Rik Godwin confirmed via social media that he had joined the project a few months ago, working in a support/consultant role.
Founded in 2017, Ubisoft Bordeaux has typically acted as a support studio for other projects, though led work on Assassin's Creed Mirage and most recently released Claws of Awaji, the one and only expansion for Assassin's Creed Shadows. Geographically, it makes sense that Bordeaux-based personnel are helping out on Beyond Good & Evil 2, which is led by Ubisoft Montpellier, situated to the south.
It's another intriguing development for Beyond Good & Evil 2 for those who have been tracking its extremely slow progress (yet progress nonetheless) in recent years, ever since it gained a new creative director, Fawzi Mesmar to steady its ship. The last while has subsequently seen work coalesce once more, with the sequel's characters given intriguing cameos in the new Beyond Good & Evil 20th Anniversary Edition, cementing a sense that the project now had a firm direction.
Then there's the fact that the project survived Ubisoft's existential reshuffle of projects, brands and development studios earlier this year — despite various other games falling by the wayside (Prince of Persia: Sands of Time Remake, we'll never forget you.)
"Needless to say, I am saddened by the cancellations that has affected my colleagues in other parts of Ubisoft and the industry," Mesmar said at the time. "I urge everyone — myself included — to offer support whenever and however they can during these times. We remain committed and focused on delivering a remarkable game for our players to enjoy."
Inexplicable as it may be, but there remains a sense that Beyond Good & Evil 2 actually still may release one day, having got this far. Exactly how it will look and whether Ubisoft ultimately chooses to keep the game's name remains to be seen. But here's hoping we will indeed see the answers to these questions, sooner rather than later.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Former Bethesda Lead Systems Designer Kurt Kuhlmann spoke to FRVR, and when he was asked about a potential Starfield sequel, he told the outlet "I don’t think Starfield was anywhere near successful enough to do a Starfield 2."
item.description:
Bethesda is still hard at work on new DLC for Starfield, but you probably shouldn't expect a sequel anytime soon.
Former Bethesda Lead Systems Designer Kurt Kuhlmann spoke to FRVR, and when he was asked about a potential Starfield sequel, he told the outlet: "I don’t think Starfield was anywhere near successful enough to do a Starfield 2."
That's not too surprising, as the game has been massively divisive since it came out, despite getting a mostly-positive review from us here at IGN. Our reviewer Dan Stapleton said: "Starfield has a lot of forces working against it, but eventually the allure of its expansive roleplaying quests and respectable combat make its gravitational pull difficult to resist."
Kuhlmann then goes on to reminisce on the ambition of Starfield, and how a sequel could have done something great, saying "It’s, in a way, too bad, because I think with the lessons learned on Starfield, a Starfield 2 could have been much closer to the game that Todd [Howard] had [in mind]." Starfield has improved a lot since it first came out, and it's still has improvements down the pipeline, but it's pretty clear that it fell short of Todd Howard's ambitions ahead of its release.
Still, Howard reiterated Starfield's support back in July, when he put out a statement saying: "As we enter Year 3, we'll continue expanding the Settled Systems with new stories, targeted gameplay improvements, and additional updates, while preparing for the launch of new Starborn content next year." It's possible that despite Kuhlmann's predictions, these updates will be able to turn Starfield around, but it's unlikely.
Instead, it seems like Bethesda is entirely focused on getting The Elder Scrolls VI out the door (even if it's still likely a couple years away), and Obsidian has been tapped to develop a new Fallout game. Even if a new Starfield game was somehow in the works, it'd be years before we ever heard about it. It's probably safe to assume that it's not going to happen any time in the near future.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Big news for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 fans today: publisher Focus Entertainment has revealed the game’s Year 3 roadmap and confirmed the new class set to hit early 2027.
item.description:
Big news for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 fans today: publisher Focus Entertainment has revealed the game’s Year 3 roadmap and confirmed the new class set to hit early 2027.
Let’s get straight to the headline here: the new class is — as so many had suspected — the Apothecary. In May I predicted the addition of the Apothecary as a heavy duty support class with a powerful healing ability, perhaps even with unique gameplay around harvesting Gene-seed.
“We’ve been following all your speculations ever since we teased the arrival of a new class, and you certainly had plenty of theories… and the majority of you were right!” Focus said. “Today, we’re finally revealing the truth: the Apothecary is joining the ranks with Patch 17 in the first quarter of 2027! We’ll disclose more info later, so stay tuned!
“Additionally, as we said in the previous Community Update, the Apothecary will receive a Champion skin in the same way the Techmarine did: in the update after its release.”
That’s all we have on the Apothecary, unfortunately, but we have plenty more on Year 3. Patch 15 hits October 1, with Patch 16 out before the end of this year. The long-awaited Chaos Siege mode, which lets you to play Heretic Astartes previously exclusive to PvP, arrives with Patch 15, as does the One-Handed Thunder Hammer. Patch 16 adds a brand-new PvP mode featuring Weekly Stratagems, just like in PvE.
2027 will being the Apothecary, as mentioned, new Operations and weapons, and “reworks to several gameplay features, with improvements coming to some of the game’s core systems,” Focus said.
“Additionally, there are a couple of other cool features that are planned, but not listed in the roadmap,” the publisher teased.
Focus also teased new customization features by saying it’s “something that will expand customization options by 33%,” and “something that will put our streaming tech to a test.”
Meanwhile, Year 3 DLC includes five new Cosmetic and Champion Packs, with the final one remaining redacted for now.
Developer Saber Interactive is of course working on Space Marine 3, which Tim Willits recently teased in an interview with IGN from gamescom. There’s no release window yet, but there’s a great deal of anticipation for it following the breakout success of Space Marine 2, which has seen over 12 million players since its 2024 launch.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: GTA 6 is getting a $400 collector's set filled with Vice City-themed goodies, but it won't include a copy of the game.
item.description:
GTA 6 is getting a $400 collector's set filled with Vice City-themed goodies, but it won't include a copy of the game.
Rockstar Games has announced a collector's set for GTA 6 known as GTA 6: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection. The $400 box will not include a copy of the game, but will include a bunch of premium merchandise, including a pair of Oakley sunglasses, a figure of a cartoon aligator, a hat, pins, stickers, and a variety of other items themed after the game's crime-ridden paradise. The set is available to preorder now through Rockstar's website and will release on November 19.
You can view the full list of items below with images.
One interesting thing to note here is that previous GTA and Red Dead games have historically always included a physical map in the standard edition of the game. We've reached out to Rockstar to see if the map is included in the boxed copies of GTA 6 or if players will have to shell out a few hundred bucks to get one.
With that said, this is a pretty pricey box set, but at least the items are of high quality. By partnering with brands like Oakley for these items, it does ensure that these aren't cheap gas station quality sunglasses that will fall apart on you in a few months. You can also likely expect that these will sell out rather quickly and be resold on eBay for absurd prices. GTA 6-themed shirts were given away at Tokyo Game Show earlier this month and have been popping up online for hundreds of dollars.
Rockstar's foot appears to be on the gas now as launch is just under two months away. After years of prolonged silence, GTA 6 has had nonstop news since June when preorders opened for the game. There has also been a new marketing beat every week since the gameplay reveal at the end of August, with the reveal of limited edition DualSense controllers and an album comprised of original music from major artists. Rockstar also recently installed a massive "Welcome to Vice City" sign in on the Miami Heat's arena in Florida, which reportedly cost the company nearly $1 million.
It's currently unclear if or when there will be another look at the game, but one last big trailer before launch doesn't seem out of the question. Some have speculated one will arrive in mid-October, possibly timed to the start of the NBA regular season. We'll have to wait and see what happens, but it seems clear that the marketing machine is only just getting started.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Domhnall Gleeson says he would have loved to have delved deeper into the "bitterness" of his Star Wars villain General Hux, before Rise of Skywalker's twist ended the character's story in surprising fashion.
item.description:
Domhnall Gleeson says he would have loved to have delved deeper into the "bitterness" of his Star Wars villain General Hux, before Rise of Skywalker's twist ended the character's story in surprising fashion.
Warning! Spoilers for The Rise of Skywalker follow...
Hux appears in all three of the Star Wars sequel trilogy films, beginning as a downtrodden sidekick for Kylo Ren, and ending up as a secret Rebel spy. Unfortunately for Hux, his last minute change of heart ultimately spells his doom — as he is quickly discovered and killed off.
It's an abrupt reveal and an even swifter demise for one of the few characters to appear in all of the sequels, though no less messy than anything else in the disappointing Star Wars Episode 9: Rise of Skywalker. And while Hux's sideplot is hardly the most pressing storyline, even Gleeson has admitted he'd previously hoped for more.
"Speaking genuinely, it would have been nice to go into the real bitterness at the heart of him," Gleeson told Liv Marks. "In a quiet way, just to find a couple of quiet moments with him, where it's not performative, where the real danger of him comes across.
"A kicked dog will end up attacking someone," he continued, "and he is a kicked dog by the end of that sort of stuff. So I would have loved to go into that stuff but, spoiler alert, I got shot in the chest by Richard E. Grant."
As part of the same interview, Gleeson said his big speech to the First Order troops was one of his easiest scenes as he knew how to fully lean into the character at such a dramatic moment. At the same time, Gleeson said his corridor conversations with Adam Driver's petulant Kylo Ren needed to worked on in the moment, in order to ensure the pair walked the fine line to make the scenes work.
Perhaps there's room for more Hux in the wider Star Wars universe of spinoff books, comics and video games? I for one would be glad to see more of Gleeson's glowering baddie, working to quietly undermine the First Order. It'd be better than what we actually got in Rise of Skywalker!
Next up for the Star Wars franchise — and sadly without Hux — Disney will finally return to the ongoing exploits of Ahsoka in a second season of Disney+ TV episodes next year. Then there's Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter, headed to theaters in May 2027. Hopes are high for both of these, after the middling response to this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu.

item.title: DC Studios has released the final Clayface trailer, which does not, thankfully, reveal his final form.
item.description:
DC Studios has released the final Clayface trailer, which does not, thankfully, reveal his final form.
Speaking to Entertainment Weekly in the summer, Clayface actor Tom Rhys Harries teased what fans can expect to see of his character’s final form when they watch the R-rated body horror movie.
“It’s been a year since I saw that thing being built out. I can’t wait for people to see it,” he says. “I’m constantly in awe of the huge creative machinery that goes into making a film like this, and how talented everybody on board is, and how lucky I felt to be a part of that in any way.”
Then, speaking to Empire magazine this week, Rhys Harries teased Clayface’s final form further, saying: “It’s f***ing sick!”
While Clayface trailers have shown how Matt Hagen becomes Clayface, with his face melting and, in one particularly disturbing shot, his eyelids fusing together, DC Studios have resisted the urge to show the Gotham bad guy in all his glory. Fans of the character from the comics and animated shows probably have an idea of what to expect here, but seeing Clayface in live-action will surely be a thrill for all.
Fans are completely on board with DC Studios holding Clayface’s final form back, as am I. The last thing you want is for the movie’s big reveal to be spoiled before the movie itself even comes out. I suspect we’ll see the final form at the end of the film as part of a setup for the character’s introduction into the wider DC Universe. Where Clayface will then appear in live-action is unknown, but you’d like to think James Gunn has a plan for the character, given he’s got his own movie.
The DCU is currently trundling forward, with the final two episodes of Lanterns out soon. We then have Clayface hitting theaters on October 23. Man of Tomorrow, Gunn’s Superman follow-up, comes out next summer. Upcoming HBO show The People v. Gorilla Grodd, which is filming now, follows.
Beyond that, we have no other confirmed DCU projects in active production, let alone with release windows. But we know there are plans for Batman, Swamp Thing, and Wonder Woman movies eventually.
As for this new Clayface trailer, there's a shot of Hagen suffocating someone inside his stomach, and you can see the head of his hapless victom protruding from his lower back (that's a bad way to go). But we also get Clayface's final form teased, briefly, at the end of the trailer via the shadow of what looks like his growing arm, his bulbous hand, and the slow rise of the monster himself.
